newsitem.title: BRAZIL: HSBC Bamerindus wins 260,000 new accounts.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Bamerindus wins 260,000 new accounts.

text.p: Deposits at Banco HSBC Bamerindus have totalled 500 million reais and 260,000 new current accounts have been opened since HSBC took over Brazil's Bamerindus late March, a bank spokeswoman said.
HSBC Holdings Plc plans to expand the bank's 2,200 branch network by opening 200 branches in the next two years, of which 100 are to be in Sao Paulo and 70 in Rio de Janeiro, she said.
The bank also aims to invest 10 million reais a year in a training scheme, the spokeswoman added.

HSBC acquired selected assets and obligations of failed Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth largest private bank and the last of the country's big banks that needed restructuring, creating a new bank which is its fully-owned subsidiary.
The Bamerindus takeover deal involved 5.7 billion reais in funds from the government's PROER program to finance mergers and buyouts in the banking sector.
So far PROER, which Brazil's Central Bank is likely to scrap by June's end, has granted 20.8 billion reais in credit lines to finance the restructuring of six banks, newspapers said.
